data.long_meaning: From the Arabic root 'kh-t-r', meaning 'to choose'. In Islamic context, Mukhtar is the chosen one, the leader, or the one who is entrusted with a mission. The name Mukhtari carries the meaning “Chosen One” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Mukhtari usually hope their child will grow to embody chosen one and live with faith, good character and purpose.

Mukhtar's most notable achievement was his successful campaign against the Umayyad governor of Egypt, 'Abd Allah ibn Zubayr, that led to the establishment of the short-lived Umayyad-Shia War. He is considered a hero and a symbol of resistance and courage in the face of tyranny and oppression for the Shia community.
